$comment: Values emitted from docs/design/design-system.manifest.json that no component reads. `scripts/verify-token-reach.mjs` fails on any emitted name that is neither read nor listed here, AND on any name listed here that a component does read — both directions, because a dead exemption is how a live one gets waved through later. Every entry carries a `why` and a `cites`, and the whole list PRINTS ON EVERY RUN rather than only on a failure: an exemption nobody reads is an exemption nobody weighs. Same shape as retired-surface.json. See F-092 and .harness/plans/F-092-a-token-that-reaches-no-pixel.md.
$groupComment: `group` is required because `xs` is a radius step AND a type step, and they are not the same decision. One of them is read by 22 `size="xs"` literals; the other is read by nothing.
$readingComment: This file is a readable inventory of what the design system has DRAWN and the product has not yet BUILT. If it grows without anyone reading it, the citations are what makes that visible — an entry nobody can justify shows up as an entry with a weak one.

unreached.why: The web target. apps/mobile is the only surface (ADR-0051), so nothing in the reader zone imports these — their only reader is emit.test.ts, which is precisely the case this check reports. They are emitted anyway because four targets from one manifest is what stops web and mobile drifting the day a web surface exists (ADR-0020). Deleting them would remove the guarantee, not the dead code. JUDGEABLE_SAMPLE joins them for F-151 and is the same case exactly: its mobile twin `nativeJudgeableSample` is read by `Pair` and `Strip`, and the CSS variable beside it is emitted for the same reason the other three web bindings are. It is worth saying what it IS, because it is the one value here that is derived rather than declared: the smallest a sample may be drawn where a screen asks you to JUDGE a colour, computed from the CIE 2° standard observer at the declared viewing distance — the same observer this product’s colorimetry uses everywhere and the one ΔE00 is parameterised for (ADR-0095). A web surface that drew a sample smaller than this would be making the mistake the mobile one no longer can.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0051 — the web target exists so four targets cannot drift

unreached.why: Emitted to CONSTRAIN, not to paint. TEXT_TOKENS is read only through its derived `TextToken` type, which is what stops `foreground.3` compiling below the large-text floor in Text.tsx. The other three are read in real code only by packages/ui/src/testing/conformance.ts, which this check deliberately does not count as a reader — that exclusion is what makes acceptance criterion 2 mean anything. A value whose job is to be checked against is a real value with no pixel, and that difference belongs here where it can be read rather than inferred. DECLARED_PAIRINGS joins them for F-171 and is the clearest case of the kind: it is the manifest pairsWith graph, emitted so the conformance suite can ask whether a pair it just found RENDERED is one gate 9 has an opinion about. Gate 9 checks the pairings the manifest declares; the suite checks that every painted colour resolves to a token; neither of them looked at a pair on a screen, so a component could draw two perfectly good tokens in a combination nothing had ever measured — and one did, 546 times. A component will never read this value, because reading it would be a component deciding whether its own colours are allowed.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0054 — emitted to constrain the type, never to paint

unreached.why: THE TRANSLUCENT DECORATIVE HAIRLINE, still painted by nothing. Every component that draws a line reaches for `border.strong` instead — the boundary of an OUTLINED control, where WCAG 1.4.11 applies directly and 3:1 is not optional. F-143 was the previous owner and did not close it, which is worth stating plainly rather than quietly re-assigning: the popover panel it added is an outlined surface and took `border.strong` like everything before it. A DECORATIVE hairline is a different thing — a rule between rows that separates without bounding, and this product has had no row list to put one between. The form controls (F-156) bring the first: a list group whose items need dividing but not enclosing. The four `.on.*` forms are permanent whatever happens to `border` itself — they are the pre-composited values the contrast gate measured, never something a component reads.

THE FOUR PRE-COMPOSITED FORMS, and what is left of an entry that also held `backdrop` itself. F-143 painted the scrim: `Popover.Overlay` takes `backdrop`, which is the first time anything in this product dimmed the page behind something — the old reason read "there is no dialog, bottom sheet or modal anywhere in the app yet", and now there is. THESE FOUR ARE DIFFERENT IN KIND RATHER THAN IN SCHEDULE, which is why they take `closedBy: null`. `backdrop.on.background` and its siblings are the values the CONTRAST GATE composited so it could measure a translucent token against each ground it may sit on — an rgba() has no contrast ratio until something is behind it. A component never reads one: it reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite. No surface will ever paint them, so no feature can close this.
unreached.permanentBecause: ADR-0044 — the .on.* forms are what the contrast gate measured, not what a component reads: a component reads the translucent token and lets the platform composite it. No surface will ever paint them.

unreached.why: ONE STEP OF A SCALE THAT IS USED, down from two. `sm`, `md`, `pill` and `swatch` are read, F-143 added `lg` for the popover panel, and F-169 gave `xl` its first reader — it is the CAP on a swatch corner, the largest corner this design system draws, which is what stops a pure ratio giving the hero an 85px curve (ADR-0094). `xs` has still found no home. That is the ordinary state of a scale: some steps have not met their surface yet, and it is a different thing from a scale that reaches NOTHING while hand-written values contradict it, which is what `nativeSpacing` was until F-095. The form controls (F-156) are where a smaller radius arrives.

ONE OF THREE, DOWN FROM THREE, AND F-152 IS WHY. This entry named F-152 as the feature that would reach these, on the strength of criterion 2 — every screen has a designed empty, loading and error state — and that is exactly what happened. `bad` is the refused photograph on AddGarment and the failed write on Export; `ok` is the write that succeeded. Before that, three outcomes on the export screen were one grey sentence, so the only difference between "your file is on the device" and "the write did not happen" was reading the words. THE PREVIOUS OWNER OF THIS ENTRY WAS WRONG TWICE AND IS WORTH KEEPING VISIBLE: it first said outfit scoring (F-031) would show the first status, and F-031 shipped without one; it then said F-149 would, and F-149 REMOVED the only reader `warn` had, because its own criterion asks for one calm readout rather than three warnings. `warn` IS THE ONE LEFT, and the reason is now a measurement rather than a schedule. The Lens describes conditions rather than judging them, so it stopped reaching for a status at all — and the obvious next home, a status beside a colour sample, is blocked: `Status` takes `adjacentToSample`, which puts it on `swatch.well`, and light `warn` measures 4.32:1 there against a floor of 4.5. So `warn` cannot be drawn in the one place it is most likely to be needed until F-174 moves it, and moving it is a design decision under a gamut ceiling rather than a lightness anybody bisects.
